title: pvContour
body:
## pvContour

Full native Contour: isosurfaces or isolines of a point scalar (cell scalar for hyper tree grids) at each value in Isosurfaces, output as polydata, with options for normals, gradients, contour-value scalars, triangle output, fast mode for image data, the 3-D strategy, point precision and point merging. Use contour for the common case with Schemaxis defaults.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Isosurfaces has no default; with an empty list the output is empty.
- For ordinary datasets the array must be point data; run cellToPoint on cell arrays.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `Contour`. Identity: `filters/Contour`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input dataset to be used by the contour filter. Accepted data: any dataset (meshes, grids, point sets) (vtkDataSet); hyper-tree grids (adaptive AMR-like trees) (vtkHyperTreeGrid). The input needs at least one point-centred array with 1 component (for vtkDataSet input). The input needs at least one cell-centred array with 1 component (for vtkHyperTreeGrid input). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkDataSet","vtkHyperTreeGrid"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ComputeGradients` | If this property is set to 1, a scalar array containing a gradient value at each point in the isosurface or isoline will be created by this filter; otherwise an array of gradients will not be computed. This operation is fairly expensive both in terms of computation time and memory required, so if the output dataset produced by the contour filter will be processed by filters that modify the dataset's topology or geometry, it may be wise to set the value of this property to 0. Not that if ComputeNormals is set to 1, then gradients will have to be calculated, but they will only be stored in the output dataset if ComputeGradients is also set to 1. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ComputeNormals` | If this property is set to 1, a scalar array containing a normal value at each point in the isosurface or isoline will be created by the contour filter; otherwise an array of normals will not be computed. This operation is fairly expensive both in terms of computation time and memory required, so if the output dataset produced by the contour filter will be processed by filters that modify the dataset's topology or geometry, it may be wise to set the value of this property to 0. Select whether to compute normals. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ComputeScalars` | If this property is set to 1, an array of scalars (containing the contour value) will be added to the output dataset. If set to 0, the output will not contain this array. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `ContourBy` | This property specifies the name of the scalar array from which the contour filter will compute isolines and/or isosurfaces. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"maxItems":2,"minItems":2,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE","REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Contourstrategy3D` | Choose the contour strategy to apply (3D case only). **IMPORTANT**: the **Use Decomposed Polyhedra** strategy generally leads to better results but can take significantly more time to complete. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Use Voxels","Use Decomposed Polyhedra"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Use Voxels"` |
| `FastMode` | This parameter controls whether to use Fast Mode or not. Fast Mode is only applicable to vtkImageData input and when GenerateTriangles is on. Fast Mode is much faster but it may produce degenerate triangles. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `GenerateTriangles` | This parameter controls whether to produce triangles in the output. Warning: Many filters do not properly handle non-triangular polygons. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Isosurfaces` | This property specifies the values at which to compute isosurfaces/isolines and also the number of such values. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1]` |
| `OutputPointsPrecision` | Select the output precision of the coordinates. **Single** sets the output to single-precision floating-point (i.e., float), **Double** sets it to double-precision floating-point (i.e., double), and **Default** sets it to the same precision as the precision of the points in the input. Defaults to ***Single***. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Single","Double","Same as input"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Single"` |
| `PointMergeMethod` | This property specifies which incremental point locator to use for handling duplicate/coincident points. | `{"type":"typed proxy","choices":["Not Merging Points","Octree Binning","Uniform Binning"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `{"type":"Uniform Binning"}` |
| `ReduceOutputMemoryUsage` | If checked, the filter will optimize the space allocated to store the contour values. This option can lower the memory consumption, especially if the output contour contains a lot of points and is generated with few contour values, at the cost of some extra computation. Note that this option will do nothing if there are more than 256 contour values. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

### Nested `PointMergeMethod` → `Not Merging Points`

Syntax: `{"type":"Not Merging Points","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `incremental_point_locators/NonMergingPointLocator`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Divisions` | Bucket counts along x, y and z inherited from the uniform point locator. Points are inserted without any duplicate search, so this has no effect on the output. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Numberofpointsperbucket` | Average bucket occupancy inherited from the uniform point locator; with direct insertion it has no effect on the output. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `PointMergeMethod` → `Octree Binning`

Syntax: `{"type":"Octree Binning","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `incremental_point_locators/IncrementalOctreeMergePoints`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Maxnumberofpointsperleaf` | Maximum number of points an octree leaf holds before it is split into eight children. Smaller values build a deeper tree (more construction work, quicker searches inside each leaf); larger values do the opposite. Affects speed and memory only. | `{"maximum":256,"minimum":16,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `16` |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Tolerance` | Distance within which a new point is treated as an existing one and merged. ParaView fixes it at 0 for this choice and hides it, as its XML instructs (always zero for merging); a positive value would also merge distinct points closer than this distance, altering the geometry. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

### Nested `PointMergeMethod` → `Uniform Binning`

Syntax: `{"type":"Uniform Binning","options":{...}}`. Native identity: `incremental_point_locators/MergePoints`. Omitted nested options retain native values on subsequent visits.

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Divisions` | Number of buckets along x, y and z of the uniform search grid used to find coincident points. It affects speed and memory only, never which points merge (only identical coordinates merge). VTK’s automatic sizing is on by default for this locator and ParaView does not expose it, so whenever the operation supplies an estimated point count the grid is sized from Number of points per bucket instead and Divisions is not used. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `PointMergeMethod.options.Numberofpointsperbucket` | Target average number of points per bucket when the bucket grid is sized automatically (bucket count = estimated point count / this value). Smaller values create more, smaller buckets. Affects speed and memory only. | `{"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvContour",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
